meta.title: Twelve weeks to a defensible study
meta.subtitle: Lane A ships on its own. Lane B is parked behind a gate, not forgotten.
meta.sizeNote: Planning weight only — the author's estimate, not a measurement.

rhythm.output: one line: what moved, what is stuck
every claim made this week gets a file or is deleted

milestones.label: Frozen artefact v1 and the Tone Gap Ledger
14 Dec — ethics and Kaposi sarcoma cutoff

weeks.laneA: PAD-UFES-20 in, smoke run, split fixed

acts.name: Landing
acts.goal: Stop shopping for datasets; start training on one.
acts.why: Every week spent comparing datasets is a week not spent on an artefact that survives inspection. This act ends with one dataset on disk, verified, and a decision written down.

acts.name: The honest model
acts.goal: One frozen artefact that survives hostile inspection.
acts.why: The contribution is not a number, it is an artefact plus the honest measurement of where it fails. Freeze early, evaluate on a population you did not train on, and publish the worst stratum in words.

acts.name: Permission
acts.why: The clinician study cannot start without a determination. A silent committee is the most likely failure in this plan, so it gets a deadline, an escalation and a published fallback.

acts.name: The clinician study
acts.goal: Show that a human plus the model changes a decision, or does not.
acts.why: A vignette study with twelve participants is underpowered and honest about it. It measures override rate, confidence shift and time to decide -- three things a reviewer can check without trusting the model's accuracy.

acts.name: The argument
acts.goal: Turn artefacts into a paper, a poster and an eight-minute demo.
acts.why: Every claim in the write-up must trace to a file. The demo's job is to make the limitations impossible to miss, including a live failure.

acts.name: Lane B — Kaposi sarcoma
acts.goal: End the pause with a real cohort, or document that it was genuinely attempted.
acts.why: Gate 1A is paused (2026-10-31) because no immediately downloadable public source contains Kaposi sarcoma. A pause is only respectable if someone is working to end it -- three routes, six weeks, written evidence either way.

gates.name: Frozen artefact — gate 1A
gates.note: Paused 2026-10-31 until a real KS cohort exists. Serving held in code.
gates.unlocks: Evaluation, calibration, the vignette study and any serving change

gates.name: Retention policy
gates.note: In force 2026-10-30, scoped to synthetic/de-identified data.

gates.name: Ethics determination
gates.note: Request prepared; four fields and a submission away.

kill.then: Train on HAM10000, evaluate on SCIN, and say so in the model card.

kill.when: SCIN turns out to have no melanoma
kill.then: Evaluate the benign head and calibration only; restate the plan, do not report a number that pretends otherwise.
Public data only, limitation in the abstract, re-apply next cycle.
Lane B becomes a protocol chapter with the email trail as process evidence.
That is the finding. Publish it with the Failure Museum; do not tune it away.

scenarios.label: KS cohort never arrives
scenarios.effect: Lane B parks after the six-week decision. The thesis ships Lane A and presents Lane B as a designed, unexecuted protocol with the email trail as process evidence.
scenarios.mitigation: Write the Lane B chapter from 5.1–5.4 as it stands: routes attempted, dates, replies, protocol sketch. Turn the pause into a documented gap.

scenarios.label: Ethics stays silent
scenarios.effect: The clinician study cannot start. Cut to eight participants if a letter lands late, or replace it with the retrospective shadow-mode analysis and say so.
scenarios.mitigation: Send 2.5 on the day 2.3 goes overdue, keep 3.8 (shadow mode) ready as the fallback, and publish the limitation in the abstract rather than hiding it.

scenarios.label: Melanoma signal too small
scenarios.effect: Reframe the contribution from detection to triage ordering plus fairness. Same artefact, honest claim.
scenarios.mitigation: Report per-class recall with n and CI, lead with the Failure Museum, and let the paper argue about ranking and calibration rather than detection.

scenarios.label: Compute too slow
scenarios.effect: Train at 160 px instead of 224, record the size in the manifest, and state the serving-time shift in the model card.
scenarios.mitigation: Cut seeds before cutting resolution, and record every configuration change in the run report so the comparison stays honest.

tasks.title: Fetch and verify PAD-UFES-20
steps: Run `bash scripts/fetch_padufes20.sh --check` and read the plan before pulling 3.35 GB
Run it with `--work ~/padufes`; rerun after any interruption — the download resumes
Read `padufes/verification.json`: 2,298 images, 1,373 patients, 1,641 lesions, per-class counts
Confirm every cancer label carries its biopsy flag and every patient a Fitzpatrick type
Convert once: `prepare_dataset.py --link hardlink --group-column patient_id`
tasks.done: 2,298 rows, patient-grouped, biopsy flags complete, skin types present
tasks.risk: The S3 zip can stall; the script resumes, so rerun rather than restart. If the archive 404s, stop and re-read the dataset page — do not substitute a dataset without recording the change.

tasks.title: DermaMNIST smoke run
steps: Inside the venv: `pip install medmnist` (20 MB npz, downloaded on first use)
One epoch through `scripts/train_model.py` — the point is plumbing, not accuracy
Confirm `runs/smoke/report.json` exists and is stamped `valid: false`
Time the run on this hardware so week 2's estimate is real
tasks.done: The pipeline trains, writes a report, and refuses to call the run valid
tasks.risk: A smoke run invites you to quote its number. It is `valid: false` by construction and never leaves the sandbox.

tasks.title: SCIN access and schema check
steps: Read the public bucket `dx-scin-public-data` and pull only the case and label CSVs
Confirm the tone columns exist and note their exact names (self-reported vs estimated)
Count how many cases actually carry a tone label — this decides the strata in 1.5
Record the licence line and whether images are reachable from here
tasks.done: The CSVs parse, the tone columns are named, and the licence line is recorded
tasks.risk: Some paths may be read-only for an anonymous reader. If images are unreachable, record that now rather than discovering it in week 4.

tasks.title: Licence register complete
steps: One row per dataset named anywhere in the repo — including the rejected ones
Each row: licence, redistribution rule, gated yes/no, adopted in this cycle yes/no
Mark every request-gated source as not adoptable this cycle, with the reason
State plainly that no downloadable public source carries Kaposi sarcoma
tasks.done: Every dataset named anywhere in the repo has a licence line and a redistribution rule
tasks.risk: A dataset named in the thesis without a licence line is a reviewer finding; the register is the cheapest defence you will ever write.

tasks.title: Data decision recorded
steps: Write the decision into the scope table in `REMEDIATION_STATUS.md`, dated
Name the training set, the evaluation set and the class that is absent
State what was rejected and why, in one line each
Anything not on the list becomes a new sprint with its own justification
tasks.done: One dated paragraph names the training set, the evaluation set and the missing class
tasks.risk: Scope creeps back if the decision is not written down; an unwritten decision is a debate you have every Monday.

tasks.title: Patient-grouped split
steps: Group by `patient_id`, never by image — 1,641 lesions over 1,373 patients
Hold out roughly a fifth of the patients, stratified by diagnosis
Write `provenance.split` into `report.json`: seed, counts, hash of the id list
Add a test that asserts no `patient_id` appears in both splits, and keep it green
tasks.done: No patient_id appears in both train and eval, and a test proves it
tasks.risk: Some releases rename a patient per visit. Check the lesion-to-patient mapping before trusting the grouping; a leaky split invalidates every number downstream.

tasks.title: HAM10000 baseline run
steps: Fetch and verify with `scripts/fetch_and_verify_ham10000.sh` (published counts or nothing)
Train one configuration end to end, 224 px, one seed first
Record command, commit sha, config and data hash inside `report.json`
Keep it as a pipeline proof and a cross-check — not the headline
tasks.done: One recorded command reproduces the run and report.json names the commit, config and data hash
tasks.risk: HAM10000 is a different population from PAD-UFES-20. Mixing the two into one headline number would be a quiet lie; use it to prove the pipeline.

tasks.title: PAD-UFES-20 run
steps: Train on the grouped split from 1.1 with the label map in `scripts/label_maps/padufes20.json`
Report per-class n and recall with confidence intervals — MEL has very few images
Add two more seeds if time allows, and report the spread instead of the best seed
Write every configuration into `report.json` and store the checkpoint outside git
tasks.done: The run reports per-class n, recall and CI, and the small MEL class is stated, not smoothed away
tasks.risk: MEL is tiny. If recall swings across seeds, say so and widen the interval; do not 'fix' it with augmented copies of the same lesion.

tasks.title: Freeze artefact v1
steps: Pick the run: the one whose report you would defend line by line
Run `scripts/freeze_model.py`; the sha256 lands in `model_manifest.json`
Set `status: frozen`, keep `serving.enabled: false`, and record the split hash
Verify from a fresh shell that the hash matches the stored file
tasks.done: status: frozen, sha256 matches the file, serving.enabled: false, verification is one command
tasks.risk: Freezing too early locks in a split you will want to change. Freeze only after the leakage test in 1.1 is green.

tasks.title: SCIN tone-stratified evaluation
steps: Score SCIN clinical images with the frozen artefact only — no retraining
Stratify by the self-reported tone column, and separately by the estimated one
Per stratum: n, the metric, and a confidence interval; empty strata are absent, not zero
Write `reports/eval_scin.json` and record the manifest hash it was computed against
tasks.done: Per-stratum n and CI are present, empty strata are absent rather than zero, and the manifest hash is recorded
tasks.risk: If SCIN carries no melanoma, a melanoma recall line would be a fiction. Restrict to the benign head and calibration, and restate the plan (kill criterion k2).

tasks.title: Tone Gap Ledger
steps: Table: stratum, n, metric, interval, gap against the lightest stratum
Bold the worst stratum and write one paragraph saying what it means
No composite fairness score — a single number hides the failure you are reporting
Link each row to the row in `reports/eval_scin.json` that produced it
tasks.done: The ledger includes the worst stratum and says in words what it implies
tasks.risk: An aggregate score invites the reader to conclude 'fair enough'. Publish the table.

tasks.title: Failure Museum, twelve cases
steps: Sample 12 errors by error type, not by which heatmap looks best
Include at least three cases from the darkest strata in the ledger
One Grad-CAM per case and exactly one sentence on why it failed
Note the licence position before publishing any image
tasks.done: Twelve cases with Grad-CAM and one honest sentence each
tasks.risk: Curating only flattering failures defeats the artefact. Fix the sampling rule before you look at the images.

tasks.title: Calibration report
steps: Reliability diagram per class, plus the calibration error, on the frozen artefact
Fit any temperature on the validation split only
Recompute on the held-out split and store before and after
State in one sentence what a confidence of 0.8 means operationally
tasks.done: Before and after calibration are both stored, and the file records which split was fitted on
tasks.risk: Fitting temperature on the evaluation split is leakage with a friendly name. The file must record the split.

tasks.title: Out-of-distribution probe
steps: Score a handful of images from a source the model never saw, at the same resolution
Record the confidence drop and what the errors look like
Write `study/ood.md`: what OOD looks like in practice, with no clinical claim
Feed the worst cases into the Failure Museum shortlist
tasks.done: The note states what the model does when the input is not from its training distribution
tasks.risk: 'It generalises well' is the trap. Report the drop, including the cases where confidence stays high and wrong.

tasks.title: Red-team day #1
steps: Take every claim you intend to make and try to falsify it in one sitting
Log each attempt, the evidence found, and the outcome: kept, weakened, withdrawn
Fix the artefacts rather than softening the wording
Date and sign the entry in `docs/RED_TEAM.md`
tasks.done: Each planned claim has an entry: attempt, outcome, and what changed as a result
tasks.risk: A red-team day that finds nothing usually means the attacks were too polite. Attack the split, the strata and the licence claims first.

tasks.title: Fill the exemption request
steps: Fill the four bracketed fields in `docs/IRB_EXEMPTION_REQUEST.md`
Read it once as a committee member looking for a reason to say no
Remove any claim the artefacts do not support (no clinical validity, no KS class)
Have the supervisor read it before it goes anywhere
tasks.done: No bracketed placeholder remains and the document claims nothing unmeasured
tasks.risk: Overclaiming in the request is the fastest way to a refusal; describe the vignette study, not a diagnostic device.

tasks.title: Submit to the committee
steps: Submit through the university channel and keep the receipt
Record the reference number, the date and the named contact in `docs/ethics/SUBMISSION.md`
Save the sent email with its attachments alongside it
Note the committee's stated turnaround, if it states one
tasks.done: A reference number and a submission date exist, and the sent email is archived
tasks.risk: A submission with no receipt is indistinguishable from a draft. The receipt is the evidence you will be asked for in week 6.

tasks.title: Determination on file
steps: Chase once at week 4, once at week 5, in writing
Store the letter as `docs/ethics/DETERMINATION.pdf` — approval or refusal, both count
Map the letter's scope onto the vignette protocol in 3.1
If refused: record the reasons verbatim and decide against kill criterion k3
tasks.done: A committee wrote something, and the protocol's scope is checked against it
tasks.risk: A verbal 'you are fine' is not a determination. Ask for it in writing while the conversation is friendly.

tasks.title: Retention scope re-check
steps: Read `SECURITY.md` §4 against what is actually on disk today
Confirm: synthetic and de-identified data only, no real patient images
Update the section if reality moved, and date the change
Link the section from the model card so a reader can find it
tasks.done: The policy still matches what is actually held
tasks.risk: A policy that describes a different repository than the one you have is worse than no policy: it reads as a claim.

tasks.title: Escalation letter
steps: One short, polite follow-up naming the 14 Dec dependency
Copy the supervisor and the named contact from the receipt
State the fallback plainly: public data only, limitation in the abstract
Log the date sent in `docs/ethics/ESCALATION.md`
tasks.done: A dated escalation exists that a reader could find in the email trail
tasks.risk: Escalation without a stated consequence reads as nagging. Name the deadline and the fallback in the same paragraph.

tasks.title: Full-approval scoping note
steps: Write the one-page shape of a full approval track: protocol, consent, data agreement
State the realistic timeline (three to six months) and that it is outside this plan
Name what would move the project onto that track — real patient images only
Keep it as a plan, not a promise
tasks.done: The note exists and explicitly keeps real patient data out of the twelve weeks
tasks.risk: Letting the full-approval track leak into week 8 is how the degree slips a year.

tasks.title: Vignette protocol fixed
steps: Fix the instrument: about 40 cases, blind, two arms, order randomised per participant
Four measures only: own decision, whether it changed, confidence 1–5, seconds to decide
State the power position honestly: twelve participants, within-subject, small effects
Freeze the wording before the pilot — wording changes after data collection are fatal
tasks.done: The wording is frozen, the four measures are defined, and the power limit is stated
tasks.risk: An instrument tuned after the first two participants cannot be analysed cleanly. Pilot, then freeze, then collect.

tasks.title: Ethics cover for the study
steps: Attach the determination (2.3) to the protocol
Check every element of the protocol against the letter's scope
If the letter is narrower, cut the protocol rather than stretching the letter
Record the mapping in `study/ethics_cover.md`
tasks.done: The study sits inside the determined scope, or the exemption covers it explicitly
tasks.risk: A scope mismatch discovered in week 8 invalidates the data you already collected.

tasks.title: Pilot with two participants
steps: Run the whole instrument with two colleagues, timing included
Watch for ambiguous wording rather than explaining it away
Fix the instrument, then re-freeze it and note the change in the protocol
Keep pilot data out of the analysis set and say so
tasks.done: Two dry runs completed, the instrument amended once, and the change is dated
tasks.risk: Pilot data leaking into the main set is a silent inflation of n. Label it and exclude it.

tasks.title: Recruit twelve participants
steps: Identify dermatologists, residents and final-year students; keep a list of roles only
No names in the repository — a participant code is enough
Book 30-minute slots across weeks 7 and 8, with two spares
Tell each person what the study is not: no patient contact, no clinical use
tasks.done: Twelve slots booked against participant codes, with no identifiers stored
tasks.risk: Recruitment slippage is the most common schedule failure in a twelve-week plan. Book spares in week 7, not week 8.

tasks.title: Run the sessions
steps: Run each session identically: same instructions, same order rule
Capture responses into `study/responses.csv` — codes, decisions, confidence, seconds
Stop immediately if a participant is uncomfortable; that is not data, it is a signal
Note any deviation from the protocol in a dated log entry
tasks.done: Twelve completed sessions, de-identified, with deviations logged
tasks.risk: Unlogged deviations are what a reviewer finds first. One line per session costs nothing now.

tasks.title: Analysis
steps: Override rate, confidence shift and time change, each with an interval
Use a paired analysis within participant; state the test and its assumptions
Report the direction of every effect, including the ones that go against you
Write `study/analysis.json` and a two-paragraph plain-language summary
tasks.done: Override rate, Δconfidence and Δtime are reported with intervals and a power caveat
tasks.risk: With n=12, a p-value is a rumour. Lead with effect sizes and intervals.

tasks.title: The unflattering arm
steps: Take eight deliberately difficult or out-of-distribution images
Score the model on them separately and report the failure rate
Keep them in the same instrument so the contrast is visible
Publish the comparison next to the main result, not in an appendix
tasks.done: A separate failure rate on hard cases is reported beside the main result
tasks.risk: Reviewers trust a paper that shows its own worst case; they discount one that does not.

tasks.title: Shadow mode (optional)
steps: Retrospective agreement only: de-identified images already in the evaluation set
No live use, no patient contact, no new data collection
Report agreement with the recorded reading, not with a clinician's live decision
Skip it without guilt if week 9 is already full
tasks.done: Either a retrospective agreement analysis exists, or the omission is recorded
tasks.risk: Shadow mode drifting into live use is the one line this project must never cross.

tasks.title: Paper draft
steps: Draft to the workshop length; one claim per paragraph
Every number gets a citation to a `report.json` path and a commit
Limitations section names the missing KS class and the single-cohort problem
Leave the abstract to last, after the numbers stop moving
tasks.done: Every number in the draft carries a file citation, and no claim outruns its evidence
tasks.risk: A number written from memory is the one an examiner checks first. Cite or delete.

tasks.title: Poster
steps: Build on the existing poster template so the disclaimers stay verbatim
One figure per claim: ledger, calibration, failure museum
The dark-skin gap gets a panel of its own, not a footnote
Print once early to check the type size at arm's length
tasks.done: Disclaimers verbatim, every figure traceable, and the gap visible without narration
tasks.risk: A poster that hides the gap looks strong for ten seconds and weak for the whole session.

tasks.title: Demo script and rehearsals
steps: Eight minutes: what it does, why, where it fails, what it cannot do, what would change that
Include one live failure from the Failure Museum and let it land
Rehearse twice — once to a colleague, once to a non-specialist
Keep an offline fallback: screenshots and a recorded run for a dead network
tasks.done: Two rehearsals completed, one with a non-specialist, and the offline fallback exists
tasks.risk: A demo that only shows successes invites exactly the question it cannot answer.

tasks.title: Reproducibility test
steps: Fresh clone on a clean machine, no cached artefacts
Run the documented command and compare against the frozen report within a stated tolerance
Record the hardware and the wall-clock time next to the result
Fix the instructions, not the numbers, when they disagree
tasks.done: A stranger reproduces the recorded result from a clean clone using only the docs
tasks.risk: 'It works on my machine' with a cached checkpoint is not reproducibility. Delete the cache first.

tasks.title: Red-team day #2
steps: Give an external reader the poster and three claims to falsify
Log attempts and outcomes in `docs/RED_TEAM.md`, dated
Withdraw or weaken any claim the artefacts cannot carry
Re-run the definition-of-done script at the end of the day
tasks.done: An external reader tried to falsify three claims and the outcome is written down
tasks.risk: Internal review finds internal problems. This one has to be somebody who owes you nothing.

tasks.title: Submit
steps: Verify the workshop deadline on its own site on the day — never from memory
Check the submission system's format requirements against the draft
Submit the Lane A paper even if Lane B is still open
Store the confirmation as `paper/SUBMITTED.md` with the date and the reference
tasks.done: A submission confirmation exists, dated, against a deadline verified that day
tasks.risk: Planning against a remembered deadline is how work misses by a week.

tasks.title: UCI / UVRI approach
steps: Two hundred words, one ask, one attachment: a one-page protocol sketch
Name the KS imaging sub-study you are asking about, with its citation
Offer co-authorship and a named collaborator on their side
Log the date, the addressee and the follow-up date in `outreach/uci-uvri.md`
tasks.done: A dated email exists with the ask, the citation and the follow-up date recorded
tasks.risk: A vague ask gets a vague no. One protocol sketch beats a page of enthusiasm.

tasks.title: Makerere dermatology meeting
steps: Request twenty minutes with the dermatology unit, not a data request
Bring one page: what the artefact does, what it cannot do, what you need
Ask which route they would trust for supervised, de-identified access
Write the answer down the same day
tasks.done: The meeting happened and the recommended access route is written down with a name
tasks.risk: A consultant supervisor converts a personal ask into an institutional one; ask for the route, not for images.

tasks.title: Consortium author contact
steps: Pick one recent African KS imaging paper with a data-sharing statement
Write to the corresponding author, citing their own protocol back to them
Ask specifically about an amendment to an existing approval
Log the contact and the response date
tasks.done: A named corresponding author has been written to, with the citation and date recorded
tasks.risk: Broadcast emails to five groups get answered by none. One careful letter beats five.

tasks.title: Ethics amendment draft
steps: Draft the amendment now so a yes does not wait on paperwork
Scope it to retrospective, de-identified images under their approval
Leave the data-transfer terms blank until a partner names them
Have it read by whoever wrote the exemption request
tasks.done: A draft amendment exists that only needs a partner's name and a signature
tasks.risk: Starting the amendment after the yes costs four to six weeks you do not have.

tasks.title: Six-week decision
steps: On 14 Dec, read the three outreach logs and decide against kill criterion k4
Write the decision with its reasons in `docs/KS_DECISION.md`, dated
If the answer is no: convert Lane B into a protocol chapter
Announce the decision in the Monday gate review the same week
tasks.done: A dated decision exists: data in hand, or the pause documented as attempted
tasks.risk: A decision nobody wrote down gets re-litigated every week. Date it and move on.

tasks.title: KS cohort ingest
steps: Same discipline as PAD-UFES-20: verify before training, never after
Check patient grouping, pathology confirmation and the licence or data agreement
Write `datasets/ks/verification.json` with counts, gaps and the agreement on file
If any check fails, stop — do not train on a cohort you cannot describe
tasks.done: The cohort verifies like PAD-UFES-20 and the data agreement is on file
tasks.risk: A cohort that arrives without an agreement is not data, it is a liability. Stop and ask.

tasks.title: Train the third class
steps: Keep the two-class frozen artefact intact while the three-class run is experimental
Retrain with KS added, grouped by patient, with per-class n and CI reported
Re-run the tone-stratified evaluation on the new artefact
Freeze as v2 only after the new ledger and museum exist
tasks.done: A three-class artefact exists with a report, a ledger and a failure museum of its own
tasks.risk: Overwriting v1 with v2 destroys the comparison the paper needs. Keep both.

tasks.title: Lift the serving hold
steps: Only after a frozen three-class artefact with its own evaluation exists
Flip `serving.enabled` in `model_manifest.json` deliberately, with the reason recorded
Re-read the serving checklist and the security section before flipping it
Update the model card and the dashboard copy in the same commit
tasks.done: The hold is lifted only where a frozen artefact and its evaluation justify it
tasks.risk: Lifting the hold to demo something is the failure mode this gate exists to prevent.
